abstract: Climate-smart agricultural (CSA) practices are central to food-system decarbonisation, yet adoption often falls short of farmers’ stated intentions, weakening the impact of incentives and extension under capacity constraints. We test whether spatially targeted, AI-generated advice can narrow this intention-action gap in a randomised field experiment with 1529 row crop farmers in Iowa, Illinois and Indiana during the cover crop decision window. Farmers assigned to receive four AI-generated emails were 4.45 %age points more likely to plant cover crops than controls (z = 2.81, p = 0.005), despite high baseline intentions in both groups. Effects operated on the extensive margin: there was no detectable change in the share of land planted among adopters. Survey responses indicate high engagement and a shift from untested optimism to more calibrated trust after exposure. Supervised AI advice can provide a low-cost, scalable complement to existing extension, improving follow-through and modestly expanding uptake without displacing human expertise.
title: AI-generated advice as a reinforcement layer in climate-smart agriculture

abstract: Relationship lending refers to lending based on close bank–borrower relationships, expected to increase credit availability and support real economic activity. This paper proposes the ST‐B filter, a novel framework identifying significant ties in temporal bipartite networks. Applying our method to Japanese financial data (1977–2021), relationship lending comprises about 10%–35% of total lending and is associated with 33% larger loan volume than transaction lending. Our method uniquely enables the analysis of relationship lending using only transaction data, without requiring detailed information on bank–borrower relationships.
journal: Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics
title: Identification of Relationship Lending in Bank–Borrower Networks

abstract: Accelerating the energy transition is pivotal to achieving sustainable economic development, yet localized environmental policies can profoundly reshape the spatial allocation of corporate capital. The impact of place-based energy transition policies on firms' cross-regional investment remains largely unexplored. Existing studies primarily examine the environmental and economic consequences of such policies, while paying limited attention to their influence on firms' geographic expansion strategies. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2006 to 2022, we examine whether and how the New Energy Demonstration City (NEDC) pilot policy affects corporate cross-regional investment (CORI). We find that the NEDC policy significantly increases firms' CORI, indicating that firms located in pilot cities expand more actively beyond their home provinces. This finding is consistent with the resource-based view. We further find that this effect is stronger for non-state-owned firms, non-heavy-polluting firms, and firms audited by the Big Four, and remains robust to a series of robustness and endogeneity tests. Mechanism analyses show that the NEDC policy promotes CORI by reducing information asymmetry and lowering corporate risk-taking. These findings suggest that place-based energy transition policies reshape firms’ geographic allocation of resources and provide new evidence on how policy-induced environmental change affects corporate investment decisions.

abstract: Embedded in the value of a statistical life (VSL) is a stream of valuations of each expected year of life. The value of a statistical life year (VSLY) has a policy-relevant role analogous to the VSL, except that it monetizes risks to short periods of life extension. This article reviews previous studies and reports new labor market estimates of the average VSLY and the variation of these values with age using two methods—inferring the average VSLY based on estimates of the VSL and a new method that provides direct empirical estimates of the valuation of a discounted life year. The direct estimates of the VSLY yield larger values than the constructed estimates. The VSLY based on fatality rates by industry and occupation is $600,000 to $800,000 at a 3% interest rate. Estimates based on age-adjusted fatality rates are somewhat lower. The discount rate used in assessing the VSLY has a pivotal effect on the estimated VSLY. The VSLY is substantially lower in the absence of discounting and more than doubled at a discount rate of 10%. Failure to use a positive discount rate greatly understates the VSLY. The article also reviews previous VSLY studies as well as estimates of the discount rate for years of life expectancy.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
title: The value of a statistical life year

abstract: We find that the effect of political connections on tax planning depends on firms’ financial conditions. After increased political connections, financially unconstrained firms increase tax planning and spending on tax services, as documented in prior studies, whereas constrained firms decrease tax planning and spending on tax services. Moreover, decreases in tax planning are only present for constrained firms that obtain new bank loans and public debt and when the connected politicians serve on banking-related committees. Our results suggest that by facilitating access to external financing, political connections reduce financially constrained firms’ use of tax planning as an internal financing tool.
journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
title: Political Connections, Financial Constraints, and Corporate Taxation

abstract: We examine whether and how firms use connected social media outlets to counteract negative coverage in traditional media. Employing a sample of Chinese listed firms with ties to social media outlets, we find that connected outlets portray firms more favorably than unconnected ones. Following unfavorable coverage in traditional media, connected outlets shift attention toward long-term prospects and promote favorable narratives, consistent with an optimism-shifting mechanism. The effect is more pronounced when firms have stronger incentives to stabilize stock prices and when managers face heightened career concerns. Our findings highlight the role of connected social media outlets in shaping corporate narratives.

abstract: This study presents results from a randomized controlled trial in Switzerland that investigates the effects of a non-monetary intervention on transport choices. A GPS-based tracking app records the movements of 814 participants for several months, and automatically detects their travel modes. The treatment consists of sending personalized transport reports to a randomly selected subgroup. These reports contain personalized descriptive and prescriptive information on participants’ transport-related external costs. The treatment reduces the external costs of transport by 12.4%, but only on weekends, and only during the first half of the study. In the second half, the effect dissipates to zero. Based on participants’ travel response and their willingness-to-pay for future reports, we estimate average gross welfare gains of 1.6–3.6 Swiss francs per participant per week in the short run. Of this, 0.8–2.8 Swiss francs reflect the private value of the reports rather than the temporary behavioral change.
journal: Journal of Environmental Economics and Management
title: Reducing transport externalities through nudging: Results from a GPS-tracked experiment

abstract: We evaluate the labor market effects of an increasing supply of high-skilled labor, resulting from a higher education expansion at established German universities. Exploiting variation in exposure across regions and cohorts, we estimate early career effects for labor market entrants. We find that high-skilled wages decline initially, particularly in non-graduate jobs, but recover over the first 5 years of experience. For graduate job takers, we even report positive wage effects after 5 years. We explain the dynamics of the effects by the interplay of several mechanisms: immediate supply effects, recovery through regional mobility, and increased productivity of graduate jobs.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
title: Early career effects of entering the labor market during higher education expansion

abstract: Aircraft payload capacity is a scarce operational resource jointly consumed by passenger body weight, non-tradable cabin and baseline baggage loads, and verified discretionary checked baggage; however, airline baggage policies typically allocate this capacity through uniform allowances and excess baggage fees. This study examines how such capacity can be allocated when passenger body weight is sensitive and privately known at the contracting stage, whereas checked baggage weight is verifiable at check-in. This study formulates a tradable payload-rights mechanism as a competitive-clearing market-design benchmark in which an airline defines the residual capacity available for verified discretionary checked baggage and passengers trade rights to carry baggage above a baseline allowance. A planner benchmark identifies the shadow price of the payload capacity. The main result establishes that under competitive trading, verifiable baggage, and market clearing, the equilibrium permit price decentralizes the planner’s benchmark allocation on the verified discretionary checked-baggage margin. The analysis separates allocative efficiency from incidence: the permit price governs the efficient allocation of scarce payload capacity, whereas the initial endowment of rights determines transfers among passengers and the division of scarcity rents between passengers and the airline. The analysis also considers implementation without direct pay-as-you-weigh pricing, emphasizing verification and settlement procedures that do not require direct body-weight reporting, airline revenue compatibility, and operational capacity shocks. The framework provides a market-design benchmark for implementing scarcity pricing on a verifiable checked-baggage margin when direct passenger-weight pricing is institutionally and socially constrained.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
title: Tradable payload rights under private passenger weight: a market-design approach to airline capacity allocation

abstract: How firms generate and select ideas influences their strategic path and the development of entire industries. To better understand this process, we experimentally analyze the impact of knowledge on idea generation and selection in an incentivized ideation task. Between treatments, we vary whether or not ideators are provided with examples of previous successful ideas before working on the task. We provide causal evidence that knowledge about such example ideas leads to path dependencies, i.e., knowledge increases the similarity of new ideas to those provided. Consistent with the hypothesis that knowledge affects the search for new ideas, we find evidence of path dependencies during idea generation, but do not find statistically significant evidence of additional path dependencies during idea selection. Overall, when knowledge is provided, we observe an increase in selected innovative ideas that are similar to previous ideas and a decrease in selected innovative ideas that are different from previous ideas.
title: An Experimental Study on the Effect of Knowledge on Idea Generation and Idea Selection

abstract: We study the proportional division value in TU-games, which distributes the grand coalition worth in proportion to the players’ stand-alone worths. Focusing on fixed-population consistency, we characterize the proportional division value through three types of axioms: axioms concerning transformations of the grand coalition worth, composition axioms, and nullified-game consistency. The first type captures how payoffs respond when the grand coalition worth changes. The composition axioms require that the outcome be the same whether a game is solved directly or through a two-step procedure based on a reference allocation and an associated adjustment of the game. Nullified-game consistency requires that, when some players’ payoffs are fixed, the solution for the remaining players in the adjusted game coincides with their original payoffs. Together with efficiency and/or fairness-related conditions where appropriate, these axioms characterize the proportional division value.
title: Characterizations of proportional division value in TU-games via fixed-population consistency

abstract: Leveraging the unique setting of unilateral euroisation, this paper examines the spillover effects of euro area monetary policy on Montenegro and Kosovo. Through the lens of a structural VAR model with block exogeneity, it shows that euro area monetary policy shocks can significantly influence output and inflation in these economies, albeit with a delayed response, while contributing only modestly to their overall business cycle fluctuations.
title: ECB monetary policy transmission to unilaterally euroised economies

abstract: In comparative case studies that select a single control using a centered pre-treatment fit criterion, researchers report a difference-in-differences interval treating the selection as fixed. Under a Gaussian panel model with known covariance, a centered criterion yields exact naive intervals when the covariance is separable with a spherical time factor, for any cross-sectional covariance. Otherwise, given the selection and an independent residual, the estimator is truncated normal; the pivot yields exact selective coverage. In our simulations, naive coverage was often conservative and never materially below nominal; working-model plug-in inference exhibited modest undercoverage under strong serial correlation.
title: Exact inference after data-driven control-unit selection in difference-in-differences

abstract: Europe's investment debate tends to ask how much capital can be mobilised and how quickly. Allocation quality also depends on who receives capital and on the spillovers their expansion creates. This column argues that for public allocation, Europe should combine simpler administration with stronger analytical capacity to recognise material anomalies in ordinary administrative information and transmit them early enough for competent authorities to assess and, where warranted, act.
abstract_zh: 欧洲的投资辩论往往关注能够动员多少资本以及速度有多快。配置质量还取决于谁获得资本以及其扩张所产生的外溢效应。本专栏认为，对于公共配置，欧洲应将更简单的行政管理与更强的分析能力相结合，以识别日常行政信息中的重大异常，并足够早地传递这些异常，使主管当局能够评估并在有正当理由时采取行动。
title: The quality of capital allocation in Europe

abstract: Increases in US electricity prices since 2020 have coincided with a sharp rise in demand from data centres. This column analyses the impact of the surge in data centre growth since 2021 on electricity prices across US utility service territories. It finds that data centres raise electricity demand and electricity prices, particularly for households. However, residential price increases are close to zero in territories served by nonprofit utilities. Policymakers should expand generation capacity, encourage data centres with flexible electricity usage, and consider tariffs on large-load customers.
abstract_zh: 自2020年以来，美国电价上涨与数据中心需求急剧上升同时发生。本专栏分析了2021年以来数据中心快速增长对美国各公用事业服务区电价的影响。研究发现，数据中心推高了电力需求和电价，尤其是对家庭而言。然而，在非营利性公用事业公司服务的区域内，居民电价涨幅接近于零。政策制定者应扩大发电容量，鼓励数据中心灵活用电，并考虑对大负荷客户征收电价附加费。
authors: Cameron Scalera, Valentina Bosetti, Filippo Pecci

abstract: During the energy crisis in 2022, electricity prices in Germany soared to unprecedented levels. To explore the drivers of the high electricity prices, we develop an electricity dispatch model that simulates hourly equilibrium prices under the assumption of perfect competition. We then extend this model to account for firms exercising market power. By comparing the outcomes of the perfect competition and Cournot competition models with actual market data, we demonstrate that market power may have contributed to higher prices during the crisis, elevating them beyond what rising input costs alone would justify.
title: Electricity prices during the energy crisis in Germany: The role of market power

abstract: We conduct a large-scale, randomized controlled trial of a six-month intervention combining intensive mentoring and group cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for youth in Chicago, following study participants for up to five years. The program was designed to engage young people at higher risk of involvement with the criminal justice system, and successfully did so with a take-up rate of 62%. Participants averaged 177 hours with mentors and nine hours of group CBT. After 24 months, youth offered the program experienced a 19% reduction in the probability of being arrested. Notably, this impact persists into adulthood, as effects remain stable through five years post-randomization. A reduction in arrests for violent offenses is driving this overall arrest reduction, with a 23% reduction in the probability of a violent-crime arrest after 24 months. The program does not impact school enrollment persistence (graduation or being enrolled), but shows suggestive improvements in school behavior and school mobility. We conclude that programs that combine mentoring and CBT can serve as a model for engaging a harder-to-reach population of youth, and can be effective in reducing criminal justice contact in the longer run.
title: Long-term impacts of youth mentoring and therapy: Experimental evidence from Chicago

abstract: Established behavioral insights may not generalize when applied to under-represented target populations. Iterative approaches that identify such external validity failures to guide policy deployment at scale and to inform subsequent design refinements gain importance. We implement this approach in a field experiment involving 1800 low-income households in one of the largest energy efficiency assistance programs. Despite extensive co-designed vetting, most behavioral insights proved ineffective or inefficient. Notably, loss-framed interventions backfired by reducing take-up. We rank insights by their Marginal Value of Public Funds (MVPF), identifying ‘unexpected winners’ that outperform alternatives rated as promising by experts and laypeople. Our analysis suggests that factors specific to low-income households, such as scarcity, fundamentally alter behavioral responses, necessitating guided deployment to optimize future public assistance design.
title: Transporting behavioral insights to low-income households: A field experiment on energy efficiency investments
